days.title: Cloud foundations and migration
days.intro: What cloud is (service and deployment models), how architects frame a cloud solution (reference architecture, cloud-native vs cloud-enabled), automating infrastructure with code, and how to move existing apps to the cloud (the 7 Rs).

topics.title: Overview of Cloud Computing
topics.overview: Learn what cloud computing is, why organisations adopt it, and how service models divide operational responsibility. Compare deployment models and the cloud-hosted, optimised and native approaches. Use these distinctions to justify a workload-specific strategy rather than assuming cloud always saves money.

sections.title: Cloud characteristics and economies of scale
Why adopt cloud: benefits, barriers, trend
Development options, myths and strategy mistakes

topics.title: Cloud Reference Architecture
topics.overview: Use reference architectures to connect business requirements to cloud components. Compare cloud-native and cloud-enabled designs, migration routes, IaC, image security and hybrid or multi-cloud placement. The worked e-commerce, gaming and recovery designs show why each component is needed.

sections.title: Architect roles and where cloud architects fit
Migration choices, Infrastructure as Code and image security
Worked reference architectures and the case for Kubernetes

topics.title: Infrastructure as Code: Vendor-Specific Examples
topics.overview: IaC defines infrastructure in versioned files rather than manual clicks. Compare provisioning, configuration and orchestration, then apply them to AWS serverless, Azure microservices, a GCP pipeline and multi-cloud Kubernetes. GitOps keeps cluster desired state in Git and synchronises it through automation.

sections.title: Vendor-native IaC: AWS SAM and Azure Bicep

topics.title: Cloud Adoption and Migration
topics.overview: Choose a migration approach by diagnosing the application’s business and technical problems. Compare VMs, containers, IaaS and PaaS, then apply the migration options and six modernisation drivers. Assess dependencies, risk and total cost, including the temporary cost bubble, before sequencing an incremental migration.

sections.title: Recap: VMs, containers, managed services and IaaS
Migration options I: Rehost and Replatform
Migration options II: Rearchitect to Encapsulate

topics.title: Day 1: What the Instructor Emphasised in Class
topics.overview: These classroom sketches connect architecture decisions, backlog work and hosting choices. Follow the same web application from on-premises tiers to cloud services and an orchestrated container design. Use the progression to explain why a component changes; the drawings are examples rather than requirements for every cloud-native system.

sections.title: From on-prem to cloud to cloud native

days.title: Persistence and cloud-native design
days.intro: Choosing where data lives: relational vs NoSQL families, CAP/BASE, polyglot persistence. Then what makes an application cloud-native (12-factor app, resilience, scalability, observability). The course spread lecture 05 across Days 1–3; it is placed here.

topics.title: Cloud Persistence
topics.overview: Choose persistence from the data shape, access pattern, consistency requirement and scale. Trace relational and object databases into the four NoSQL families, then compare sharding, replication and eventual consistency. Map local, file, block, object and database storage to cloud services while accounting for the operating cost of multiple stores.

sections.title: Why persistence matters in the cloud
Big data and the birth of NoSQL
The four NoSQL data store patterns
Choosing a store: KV, column, document, graph, NewSQL
Cloud persistence options: file storage types

topics.title: Architecting a Cloud Native Application
topics.overview: Design services for elasticity, resilience, automation and observable operation. Start with state placement and the 12-factor practices, then connect immutable delivery, external configuration and orchestration. Use the design checklists to test scaling, availability, security, operations and feasibility against actual requirements.

sections.title: Maturity, traditional vs cloud native, summary

days.title: Containers, Kubernetes, styles and microservices
days.intro: Running cloud-native apps: containers and Kubernetes, when to use vendor-managed services instead, the main application architecture styles (monolith, microservices, event-driven, serverless, lambda/kappa…), and how to decompose and design microservices.

topics.title: Kubernetes: A Simple Introduction
topics.overview: Kubernetes schedules container workloads and reconciles them toward declared state. Learn the control-plane and worker roles, then connect Pods, Deployments, Services, Ingress, storage and configuration. Compare local and managed clusters, and distinguish the automation Kubernetes supplies from the availability and security choices you must design.

sections.title: Running K8s: Minikube, YAML and cloud
Design patterns, state and traffic flow

topics.title: Vendor Managed Services
topics.overview: Map an architectural need to a managed-service category, then to a provider example. Compare compute, storage, networking, data, messaging and security across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. Similar categories help comparison, but service semantics and customer responsibilities still need checking.

topics.title: Application Architecture Styles (Archetypes)
topics.overview: Choose architecture styles from quality attributes, data needs and team capacity. Compare frontend options, monoliths, microservices, hexagonal design, serverless, and Lambda/Kappa data processing. The modern archetypes add decisions about blast radius, placement, ownership, offline work and repeatable operations; combine them only where their benefits justify the cost.

sections.title: Industry context and full stack layers

Choosing an architecture and architectural thinking
Lambda, Kappa, IoT, event-driven, multi-cluster, AI
Modern composables, scale cube and evolution

Appendix: local-first, MACH, platform engineering, selection

topics.title: Microservices Design
topics.overview: Decompose services around business capabilities and define their APIs, data ownership and collaborations. Compare synchronous calls, messaging, REST and gRPC, then connect gateways, discovery, versioning and maintenance. Adopt the extra distributed-system complexity only where independent delivery or scaling provides enough benefit.

sections.title: When microservices fit and how to migrate
API gateway, versioning and service discovery

topics.title: What the Instructor Emphasised in Day 3: Kubernetes, Toolchains and Architecture Styles
topics.overview: These sketches connect Kubernetes control-plane roles, delivery-toolchain choices and application styles. Read the modernisation examples as options rather than mandatory replacements. The key architectural decisions are where durable state lives, how capability boundaries are drawn and which scaling mechanism addresses the actual bottleneck.

Architecture style classification and scaling map

days.title: Serverless, generative AI and security
days.intro: Serverless computing (FaaS, triggers, cold starts, when it fits), integrating GenAI into cloud-native apps (managed model APIs vs self-hosting, RAG, agents), and cloud security (shared responsibility, identity, data protection). The afternoon was the class test.

topics.title: Serverless Architecture
topics.overview: Serverless shifts function-server operations to a provider while the application still needs sound state, error and security design. Choose it for suitable event-driven work, and compare function, gateway, queue, stream and legacy-proxy patterns. Learn the Lambda configuration and invocation model without treating the lecture’s pricing details as permanent limits.

sections.title: Design principles and when to use serverless
Layers of abstraction and serverless compute and data services

topics.title: Integrating Generative AI Tools into Cloud Native Applications
topics.overview: Connect the Transformer’s attention mechanism to practical uses of language models. Compare a plain model call, retrieval-augmented generation and tool-using agents, then place them in the GenAI stack. Choose the simplest pattern that supplies the context or actions the application needs, with a clear business benefit.

sections.title: LLM vs RAG vs Agents, and what GenAI is
Model families, value and the GenAI stack

topics.title: Cloud Security: An Overview
topics.overview: Analyse a cloud threat by its affected security property, responsible party and relevant control. Apply shared responsibility across service models, then protect data, applications and identities through their lifecycle. Use the lecture’s historical cases to connect prevention with monitoring, audit and recovery rather than assuming a cloud model is inherently secure.

sections.title: Shared responsibility, enterprise concerns and CSA
